02.event: He once ruled in accordance with Rabbi Elazar's view about a woman's menstrual impurity.
02.turn: Afterward he remembered that Rabbi Elazar's colleagues disagree with him.
02.outcome: He still said Rabbi Elazar may be relied upon in exigent circumstances.
02.summary: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi once issued a ruling following Rabbi Elazar. Later he remembered that others disagreed with Rabbi Elazar. He nonetheless declared that Rabbi Elazar's view can be relied on in a pressing situation.

03.actor: A steward appointed for a dead man's orphans, before Abaye
03.event: A man had designated a field as a marker for another, contested it, and died; his steward came to Abaye, who said the deceased had forfeited his right.
03.turn: The steward argued the father could have claimed he only meant one furrow, and then that he had bought the land back; Abaye accepted both claims.
03.outcome: Abaye awarded the furrow with its palm trees to the orphans and praised the steward as the kind one should appoint.
03.summary: A man who had marked a field as belonging to another later contested it and died, leaving a steward over his orphans. Abaye told the steward the right was lost. The steward argued that the father could have claimed he only gave one furrow, then that he had bought it back, and Abaye accepted each, giving the orphans the furrow with its palm trees. He said one should appoint a steward like this one.

05.event: Rabbi Elazar taught that the uneducated will not be revived; Rabbi Yohanan objected and Rabbi Elazar defended it from another verse.
05.turn: Rabbi Elazar saw that Rabbi Yohanan was grieved for common people.
05.outcome: He offered them a remedy: those who support Torah scholars are credited as cleaving to the Divine Presence.
05.summary: Rabbi Yohanan told Rabbi Elazar that God would not be pleased with his teaching that ordinary people will not be revived. Rabbi Elazar defended it with another verse. Seeing Rabbi Yohanan's distress, he offered a remedy: whoever marries his daughter to a scholar or supports scholars is counted as cleaving to God.

07.event: Several sages became impotent from Rav Huna's discourse, and Rav Aha bar Ya'akov was afflicted by a disease of holding back urination.
07.turn: They hung him from the cedar column of the study hall and a green substance came out of him.
07.outcome: He was healed and said that of sixty elders he alone avoided the damage.
07.summary: Rav Giddel, Rav Helbo and Rav Sheshet became impotent from sitting through Rav Huna's discourse. Rav Aha bar Ya'akov was afflicted too, but was hung from a cedar column and a green substance emerged, healing him. He said that of sixty elders he alone escaped.

08.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and his son
08.event: Rabbi's first match for his son ended when the bride died; then his son married into Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra's family after changing his plan to study first.
08.turn: The bride's death made Rabbi fear a family flaw, and the son, seeing the new bride, switched from studying first to marrying first.
08.outcome: Lineage was found sound (both from David's family); the son married, studied twelve years, and his wife who had become infertile was healed by prayer.
08.summary: Rabbi arranged his son's match with Rabbi Hiyya's family but the girl died, so they checked the families' ancestry and found both descended from David's line. He then arranged a match with Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra's family, where the son, on seeing the bride, cut his planned study years and married first, ashamed before his father, who reassured him. After twelve years of study his wife was infertile and she was healed through prayer.
08.missing: The passage joins two separate episodes; the ending of the second is in context segment [7].

09.event: Avimi honored his father Rabbi Abbahu, running to open the door for him, and one day his father asked for water.
09.turn: His father dozed off before he brought it.
09.outcome: Avimi stood bent over him until he woke, and was rewarded with success in interpreting a psalm.
09.summary: Avimi, already ordained with five sons, would run to open the door whenever his father Rabbi Abbahu knocked, calling out 'yes, yes'. One day his father asked for water and fell asleep before it came. Avimi stood bent over him until he woke, and was helped to interpret the psalm 'A song to Asaph'.

10.actor: The orphans who divided the estate, and Rav Yosef and Abaye
10.event: A man left a palm tree to his daughter, the heirs divided the estate without giving her one, and Rav Yosef compared it to the mishna.
10.turn: Abaye distinguished the cases: the tree is held by all the heirs.
10.outcome: Abaye ruled they must give her a tree and redivide the estate.
10.summary: A man willed a palm tree to his daughter, but the orphans divided the property and gave her none. Rav Yosef thought this was like the mishna's case. Abaye replied the cases differ because the tree is in the heirs' possession, and told them to give her a tree and divide again.
10.missing: It is a legal case and ruling rather than an event with a human turn; the actual outcome is a recommended remedy, not a reported result.

12.actor: A man who deposited pearls, before Rabbi Ami
12.event: A man deposited seven pearls tied in a sheet in the house of Rabbi Meyasha, who died without instructions.
12.turn: The family and the depositor came before Rabbi Ami in dispute over ownership.
12.outcome: Rabbi Ami ruled for the depositor because Meyasha was not wealthy and the man gave a distinguishing mark.
12.summary: A man left seven pearls tied in a sheet with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without saying whom they belonged to. The matter went to Rabbi Ami, who said Meyasha was not wealthy enough to own them and the claimant had given an identifying mark. He ruled the pearls belonged to the depositor.

13.actor: Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law, and the sages Ameimar, Mar Zutra, Rav Ashi and Rav Gamda
13.event: Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebelled against her husband while holding a garment, and three sages ruled she had lost her worn clothes.
13.turn: Rav Gamda accused them of flattering Rav Zevid, since Rava had left the question unresolved.
13.outcome: The conclusion: since it was not decided either way, what she seized is not taken from her, and what she did not seize is not given.
13.summary: Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebelled against her husband and held on to a garment. Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi ruled she had lost her worn clothes. Rav Gamda charged them with deferring to the great Rav Zevid, since Rava never resolved the point. The result was that she keeps what she seized and gets nothing she did not.

14.event: A woman came before Ameimar asking for her one-tenth of the estate while her brothers said they would pay her off in cash if they had money.
14.turn: Ameimar stayed silent at their remark.
14.outcome: This was taken to show he retracted and treated her as a creditor.
14.summary: Rav Minyumi recounts standing before Ameimar when a woman came asking for a tenth of her father's estate. Her brothers said that if they had money they would remove her by paying cash, and Ameimar said nothing. From his silence it was concluded he had retracted his view and held she was only a creditor.
14.missing: The passage mainly states a legal opinion; the anecdote is brief and its point is inferred.

16.event: Nehemya was so absorbed in learning that he went out beyond his Shabbat limit.
16.turn: Rav Hisda told Rav Nahman his student was in distress outside the limit.
16.outcome: Rav Nahman advised making a human partition so he could reenter.
16.summary: Nehemya, deep in study, wandered beyond the Shabbat limit. Rav Hisda told Rav Nahman that his student was stranded and in distress. Rav Nahman said to form a wall of people for him to walk through and so return.

17.actor: A maidservant of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household
17.event: She immersed, and a bone was found between her teeth after she came up.
17.turn: The bone showed an obstruction to the immersion.
17.outcome: Rabbi required her to immerse again.
17.summary: A maidservant in Rabbi's household immersed herself, and afterward a bone was found between her teeth. Rabbi required her to immerse again.
17.missing: The incident is cited only as a proof in a legal question; the passage itself is mainly argument.

18.event: After his wedding he went off and studied for twelve years.
18.turn: On his return his wife had become infertile.
18.outcome: He pleaded for mercy and she was cured.
18.summary: Rabbi arranged a match for his son with Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra's family, and the son married and then spent twelve years in the study hall. When he came back his wife was infertile. Divorcing her or marrying another would have shamed her, so he prayed for mercy and she was healed.

19.event: Rabbi Elazar doubted Rav Beruna's report of Shmuel's ruling and went to Shmuel to check.
19.turn: Shmuel confirmed it, and Rabbi Elazar challenged him with Shmuel's own statement about the wording of the mishna.
19.outcome: Shmuel was silent and did not answer.
19.summary: Rav Beruna taught a ruling in Shmuel's name and Rabbi Elazar doubted it, so he had Beruna show him Shmuel's lodging. Shmuel confirmed the ruling to his face. Rabbi Elazar then objected that Shmuel himself had said the law follows the mishna's wording, and Shmuel just fell silent.

20.event: Ravina saw a man tie his donkey to a palm tree on Shabbat and protested, but the man ignored him.
20.turn: Ravina declared the man excommunicated in Rav Ashi's presence, then asked if that appeared irreverent.
20.outcome: Rav Ashi told him that where God's name is desecrated no honor is paid to a teacher.
20.summary: While sitting before Rav Ashi, Ravina saw a man tie his donkey to a palm tree on Shabbat. He protested and was ignored, so he pronounced the man excommunicated. He then asked Rav Ashi whether that looked irreverent, and Rav Ashi said that when God's name is being profaned, one does not defer to a teacher.
